subject: Geopolitics
title: Tech Alliances
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Tech Alliances.

hook.text: The US, Netherlands, and Japan formed a chip alliance. Their goal: deny China access to advanced semiconductors.

buildup.text: Technology alliances coordinate export controls, research sharing, and industrial policy among trusted partners.

discovery.text: In a tech-driven world, who you share innovation with matters more than who you share soldiers with.

twist.text: Tech alliances create new exclusions. Countries cut off from chip supply chains are cut off from the future.

climax.text: The 21st-century alliance system may organize around tech supply chains more than military threats.

punchline.text: The new iron curtain is made of silicon.

quiz.question: Why are technology alliances becoming geopolitically important?
options: Technology has replaced military spending entirely
Controlling innovation sharing matters more than troop deployments
Only allied nations can produce electronic goods
